title: Van der Westhuizen named to CSC Academic All-America First Team
text:
Van der Westhuizen named to CSC Academic All-America First Team
Rice women's track and field athlete Mckyla Van der Westhuizen was named to the College Sports Communicators (CSC) Academic All-America First Team, the organization announced on July 15. This recognition adds to Van der Westhuizen's list of achievements during her time at Rice University.
"Once again, McKyla shows why she is one of the best to ever come out of the women's track and field program," said Rice head coach Andrea Blackett. "She is not only in a class by herself on the field but also in the classroom. This honor truly demonstrates what a remarkable young woman she is. We are so proud to have had her here with us and proud of the way Coach Brek Christensen inspired her and developed her amazing talent."
Van der Westhuizen graduated this year with a degree in Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology, finishing with a 3.75 GPA. In 2024, she was named to the CSC Academic All-America Second Team. She has also earned three USTFCCCA All-Academic honors and was recognized as an American Conference Scholar Athlete of the Year.
Her athletic accomplishments include becoming Rice women's track and field's first national champion in 24 years after setting a school record throw of 60.87 meters, securing first place on her final attempt at nationals. Van der Westhuizen concluded her collegiate career with three consecutive First Team All-American honors and four overall.
She claimed the American Conference javelin title for three straight seasons, contributing to Rice's first American Championship team victory. In addition, Van der Westhuizen received the Joyce Pounds Hardy Award in 2025.
